subject: Post-call: capacity guardrails, streaming windows, and token-rate calibration
content:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jensen <alex.jensen@fastlane.ai>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@fastlane.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: capacity guardrails, streaming windows, and token-rate calibration

Hi Alex / Jordan —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment before the sizing exercise:

Summary of asks (from FastLane AI):
- Primary use: interactive chat and a streaming summarization endpoint for live call transcripts.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile token response <= 200 ms for chat; tail for streaming piece should keep first-byte under 500 ms and steady-state per-token under 120 ms.
- Typical session shape: 60% of sessions are short chat (avg 40 tokens), 30% are medium (avg 250 tokens), 10% are long streaming sessions (avg 10k tokens over 10–20 minutes).
- Concurrency: expected concurrent active sessions 350 steady-state with bursts up to 1,400 concurrent sessions in a 5–10 minute crest during business-critical windows.
- QPS / tokens: baseline QPS ~40 requests/sec (mostly short chats), expected token throughput baseline ~12k tokens/sec; crest tokens/sec estimate up to ~85k tokens/sec during peak promotions.
- Persistence and KV cache: streaming summaries will benefit from aggressive KV caching per session; customer will supply conversation IDs to enable prefix reuse.

Attachments: I dropped the quick workload snapshot we pulled from your call logs (workload-snapshot.csv) and a lightweight SLO template (redwood-slo-template.pdf) so we can capture the SLO language you want included.

Immediate next steps we recommended on the call:
1) FastLane to validate the crest window definition and share a 7-day hourly token histogram (we'll use the CSV shape to simulate burst packing).
2) Redwood to run a preliminary slotting exercise (quantized capacity buckets) and return a cost/latency tradeoff matrix for three configurations (low-cost quantized, balanced, low-latency).
3) Schedule a follow-up 30-min ops deep-dive next week to walk the simulation results — propose Wed 09/23 10:00 PDT.

Marissa / Priyom: can you run a quick back-of-envelope mapping from their crest token/sec (85k) and concurrent streaming profiles to recommended slot counts and whether we need multi-region fallbacks to hit the 95th p95 numbers above? I flagged that streaming sessions are heavy on KV cache benefits so include assumptions about cache hit rates (80% / 90% scenarios).

Alex — appreciate the high-level numbers; once you confirm the 7-day histogram and the crest window times (local timezone is ET), we can finalize the simulation inputs.

Best,

Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0129
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Jensen <alex.jensen@fastlane.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@fastlane.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 09:08:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: capacity guardrails, streaming windows, and token-rate calibration

Thanks Monica — good summary. A couple clarifications from our side:

- Crest definition: for us a crest is any 10-min window where token/sec > 65k — the big marketing pushes create a sharp 6–12 minute crest.
- The 10k token streaming sessions are mostly during webinars where 50–80 concurrent streams run; these sit on dedicated endpoints today.
- We can export the 7-day hourly histogram by EOD tomorrow; will include per-minute breakdown for the recent two promotion days.

Question: can Redwood simulate an 80% KV cache hit vs 60% hit? Our current infra gives us around 65–70% with naive prefixing; if you show the delta at 60/80/90% that helps us prioritize engineering work on prefix reuse.

We also want to understand estimated 99th-percentile CPU/GPU utilization per slot in the low-latency config — if you can include that in the matrix that would be ideal.

Alex
Alex Jensen
Head of Platform, FastLane AI
alex.jensen@fastlane.ai | +1 (617) 555-2391

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Jensen <alex.jensen@fastlane.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: capacity guardrails, streaming windows, and token-rate calibration

Agree with Monica's summary and Alex's asks — I'll take the simulation inputs. Quick notes on assumptions I'll run with (will document in the matrix):

- Baseline token processing latency per-token (balanced config): 0.18 ms/token effective (this maps to ~180 ms on 1k-token responses at steady-state; adjust for shorter responses).
- Low-latency config will target optimized kernels + tighter batch windows, raising cost by ~1.9x but targeting 95th per-token ~0.12 ms/token.
- Cache hit scenarios: simulate 60%, 80%, 90% cache-hit. For streaming sessions assume KV-cache warmup latency penalty in first 10–20 tokens.
- Burst packing: we'll simulate 5/10/20-second batching windows to see latency vs throughput tradeoffs at crest.
- Concurrency mapping: assume average concurrent GPU slots can host ~14 steady short sessions or ~2 long streaming sessions depending on memory and kv cache residency.

Deliverables by Wed 09/23 EOD (internal):
- Capacity slot recommendations for the three configs (low-cost / balanced / low-latency) with cost estimates.
- Simulation workbook (CSV) and a short note on sensitivity to KV hit rate.
- Suggested follow-up agenda for the customer deep-dive.

Priyom — can you pull the slot-performance numbers from the last benchmark set (June compile) and attach the short table I mentioned? I'll assemble the deck.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jensen <alex.jensen@fastlane.ai>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@fastlane.ai>

Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: capacity guardrails, streaming windows, and token-rate calibration

Appreciate the quick answers Alex. Confirming our proposed follow-up:
- Ops deep-dive: Wed 09/23 10:00 PDT (30 mins) — I'll send a calendar invite once Alex confirms the per-minute histogram time slice.
- Deliverables from Redwood by EOD 09/23: preliminary slot matrix + cost/latency tradeoffs + simulation CSV.

Alex — once you share the histogram and the specific crest windows (ET), we'll make sure multi-region fallback options are explicitly modeled if a US-only deployment can't meet the tail SLOs during crest.

Thanks — looking forward to the next call.

Monica
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0129
